name: Network Security
summary: Scanning, enumeration, traffic capture and analysis for network assessments
description: A toolkit for assessing networks you are authorized to test: port and service scanning, host discovery, SMB/SNMP/DNS enumeration, packet capture and analysis, traffic generation and bandwidth monitoring. Pairs well with the Sniffing and Spoofing tools and underpins both the Red Team and Blue Team profiles.

tools.name: Nmap
tools.summary: Network exploration tool and security/port scanner

tools.name: MASSCAN
tools.summary: Asynchronous TCP port scanner for large address ranges

tools.name: ZMap
tools.summary: Single-packet network scanner for Internet-wide surveys

tools.name: arp-scan
tools.summary: Discover and fingerprint IP hosts on the local network with ARP

tools.name: netdiscover
tools.summary: Active and passive ARP reconnaissance of local networks

tools.name: fping
tools.summary: Send ICMP echo requests to many hosts in parallel

tools.name: hping3
tools.summary: Assemble and send custom TCP/IP packets, and trace responses

tools.name: DNSRecon
tools.summary: Enumerate DNS records, zones and subdomains of a domain

tools.name: dnsenum
tools.summary: Enumerate DNS information and attempt zone transfers

tools.name: fierce
tools.summary: Locate non-contiguous IP space and hostnames for a domain

tools.name: DNS lookup utilities
tools.summary: dig, delv and nslookup DNS query clients from BIND 9

tools.name: smbmap
tools.summary: Enumerate SMB shares and permissions across a network

tools.name: smbclient
tools.summary: Command-line client for SMB/CIFS file and print shares

tools.name: nbtscan
tools.summary: Scan networks for NetBIOS name information

tools.name: onesixtyone
tools.summary: Fast SNMP scanner that brute-forces community strings

tools.name: SNMP utilities
tools.summary: Net-SNMP command-line tools such as snmpwalk and snmpget

tools.name: LDAP utilities
tools.summary: OpenLDAP clients for querying directory services (ldapsearch)

tools.name: Wireshark
tools.summary: Graphical network protocol analyser
tools.notes: Capturing needs permission to the interface; Debian's dpkg-reconfigure wireshark-common sets up the 'wireshark' group so you need not run it as root.

tools.name: TShark
tools.summary: Command-line version of the Wireshark protocol analyser

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.summary: Command-line network packet capture and inspection

tools.name: termshark
tools.summary: Terminal user interface for tshark, in the style of Wireshark

tools.name: ngrep
tools.summary: Grep-like matching across live or captured network traffic

tools.name: netsniff-ng
tools.summary: High-performance packet capture and networking toolkit

tools.name: iPerf3
tools.summary: Measure achievable bandwidth on IP networks

tools.name: iftop
tools.summary: Show bandwidth usage per connection on an interface

tools.name: mtr
tools.summary: Combined traceroute and ping network diagnostic

tools.name: traceroute
tools.summary: Trace the route IPv4/IPv6 packets take to a host

tools.name: assetfinder
tools.summary: Find domains and subdomains related to a given domain

tools.name: bettercap
tools.summary: Modular network attack and monitoring (MITM) framework
tools.notes: Many modules need root and a capable interface; run only on networks you are authorized to test.

tools.name: Ettercap (GUI)
tools.summary: Sniffer, interceptor and logger for switched LANs
tools.notes: Active interception (ARP poisoning) needs root and authorization; the command is the same binary as the console build.

tools.name: Scapy
tools.summary: Interactive packet manipulation, crafting and sniffing in Python

tools.name: Ncat
tools.summary: Nmap's netcat with SSL, proxy and broker support

tools.name: tcpflow
tools.summary: Capture and reconstruct the data streams of TCP connections

tools.name: Recon-ng
tools.summary: Full-featured web reconnaissance framework

tools.name: Sherlock
tools.summary: Hunt down social-media accounts by username across sites

tools.name: Shodan CLI
tools.summary: Command-line client and library for the Shodan search engine
tools.notes: Needs a Shodan API key (shodan init <key>); queries use your own account's credits.

external.name: Amass
external.summary: In-depth attack-surface mapping and subdomain enumeration
external.license: Apache-2.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: OWASP Amass is a Go tool released on its own cadence and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install the release binary from the Amass releases page, or build with 'go install github.com/owasp-amass/amass/v4/...@master'.

external.name: subfinder
external.summary: Passive subdomain discovery from many data sources
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: ProjectDiscovery's subfinder is distributed as Go release binaries outside Debian.

how.text: Download the release binary for your architecture, or build with 'go install' (Go is in Debian). See the ProjectDiscovery install docs.

external.name: httpx (ProjectDiscovery)
external.summary: Fast, multi-purpose HTTP toolkit and prober
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian (the Debian 'httpx' name is an unrelated Python library).

why.text: The ProjectDiscovery httpx prober is a Go binary not in Debian; Debian's python3-httpx is a different project.

how.text: Install with 'go install github.com/projectdiscovery/httpx/cmd/httpx@latest', or download a release binary.

external.name: naabu
external.summary: Fast SYN/CONNECT port scanner from ProjectDiscovery
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: naabu is a Go tool released outside Debian and needs libpcap at build time.

how.text: Install with 'go install github.com/projectdiscovery/naabu/v2/cmd/naabu@latest', or download a release binary.

external.name: gowitness
external.summary: Screenshot web pages and services from the command line
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: gowitness is a Go tool distributed as release binaries; it drives headless Chrome.

how.text: Download the release binary for your architecture, or build with 'go install' (Go is in Debian).

external.name: Aquatone
external.summary: Visual inspection of websites across many hosts
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: Aquatone is a Go tool distributed as release archives outside Debian.

how.text: Download the release archive for Linux and place the binary on PATH; a Chromium/Chrome is required.

external.name: RustScan
external.summary: Very fast port scanner that hands results to Nmap
external.license: GPL-3.0 (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: RustScan is distributed as a .deb on its releases page and as a crate, but is not in Debian itself.

how.text: Install the official .deb from the RustScan releases page, or build with 'cargo install rustscan'.

external.name: theHarvester
external.summary: Gather emails, names, subdomains and hosts from public sources
external.license: GPL-2.0 (open source); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: theHarvester is maintained on PyPI/GitHub and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install theHarvester'), or run from a git checkout.

external.name: mitmproxy
external.license: MIT (open source); not currently in Debian trixie.

why.text: mitmproxy ships prebuilt bundles and PyPI wheels on a fast cadence and is not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Install into an isolated environment with pipx ('pipx install mitmproxy'), or use the official standalone binaries.

external.name: Snort
external.license: GPL-2.0 (open source); Snort 3 is not in Debian trixie.

why.text: Snort 3 is distributed by Cisco/Snort.org outside Debian; Suricata, which is in Debian, is an alternative.

how.text: Build Snort 3 from the official source release, or use the vendor packages per the Snort docs.

external.name: NetworkMiner
external.summary: Passive network forensic analysis of PCAP files

why.text: NetworkMiner is closed-source .NET software and cannot be redistributed by Shadow OS.

how.text: Download the free edition from Netresec and run it under Mono/.NET on Linux.

why.text: Maltego is closed-source commercial software and cannot be redistributed by Shadow OS.

how.text: Download the installer for Linux from Maltego and register for a Community or commercial account.

external.name: SpiderFoot
external.summary: Automated OSINT collection and correlation engine
external.license: MIT (open source); not packaged in Debian.

why.text: SpiderFoot is a Python application distributed on GitHub and not in Debian trixie.

how.text: Clone the official repository and run ./sf.py after installing its Python requirements, ideally in a virtualenv.
